newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 12.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on March 12. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Suharto said the Indonesian Constitution does not allow opposition.

Armed forces chief General Feisal Tanjung said the military would stick to its dual defence and sociopolitical functions for the foreseeable future. He said the military's dual function doctrine was part of the concensus of the nation to which the armed forces had devoted its life.

The ASEAN Chambers of Commerce and Industry supports ASEAN 2020 economic vision of eradicating poverty and increasing the region's share in world trade. ASEAN, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

Indonesia's flag carrier Garuda Indonesia has signed a strategic alliance with Sempati Air, which is expected to include cooperation in services and marketing as well as aircraft maintenance, including ground handling.

Private financing firm PT Dua Satu Tiga Puluh (DSTP) has officially opened its share offering to public, seeking to collect around $1.1 billion to finance the development of the N-2130 jet programme of state-run plane maker Industri Pesawat Terbang Nusantara (IPTN).

State Minister of Research and Technology Jusuf Habibie said the government will conduct further studies on the need for nuclear energy in Indonesia. He said the use of such energy will be postponed from the previously planned year 2003 until 2020 or even 2030.
